version.changelog:
- Initial release of the Pakt Escrow API skill, providing on-chain escrow management for agents.
- Supports creating, managing, and releasing escrow contracts on supported EVM chains using the @pakt/psilo SDK.
- Two authentication/wallet options: SIWA (for agent-only endpoints and onchain receipts) or Evalanche (for simple, multi-EVM wallets).
- Clear instructions and code examples for registering/authenticating agents, initializing the SDK, and performing escrow operations.
- Details all available escrow operations: get supported chains/assets, create escrow, query status, prepare buyer/seller updates, and arbiter-controlled release.

llm.summary: The skill's description (on‑chain escrow) matches the instructions, but the SKILL.md requires wallets, private keys, filesystem persistence, and installing third‑party npm packages without declaring those credentials or config paths — that mismatch is concerning.

dimensions.detail: The skill's stated purpose is on‑chain escrow via the @pakt/psilo SDK which is coherent, but the skill metadata declares no required credentials or config while the instructions clearly require an agent wallet, signing capability, and an API base URL (ESCROW_API_URL). The absence of declared wallet/private‑key requirements is a mismatch.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent to broadcast on‑chain registration transactions, request/verify SIWA nonces, sign SIWA messages with the agent wallet, and use Evalanche which creates a wallet file (e.g. ~/.evalanche/keys/agent.json). Those are sensitive operations (signing, broadcasting transactions, writing/reading private keys) and go beyond simple API calls; yet the metadata does not surface these scope requirements.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill is instruction‑only (no install spec), but directs installing npm packages (@pakt/psilo and evalanche). Installing unvetted npm packages at runtime is a moderate risk (supply‑chain / arbitrary code). This is expected for an SDK‑based skill, but the registry metadata does not document or pin package sources/versions beyond the prose.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Declared requirements list no env vars or credentials, yet SKILL.md references process.env.ESCROW_API_URL and implicitly requires private keys / wallet files (or SIWA receipts/JWTs). Requiring private keys or persistent wallet files without declaring them is disproportionate and obscures the secrets surface.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The instructions expect creation/use of persistent wallet files (e.g. ~/.evalanche/keys/agent.json) and on‑chain registration (which ties to a persistent agent identity). The skill metadata does not declare config path access. While always:false (no forced inclusion), the runtime behavior will persist secrets/config on disk unless the implementer takes care.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to be what it says (an escrow SDK wrapper) but it asks you to create and use agent wallets, sign transactions, and install third‑party npm packages — none of which are declared in the skill metadata. Before installing or running it: 1) verify the npm packages (@pakt/psilo, evalanche) on the registry (maintainer, versions, source code, and recent downloads); 2) prefer using a testnet and disposable wallet (not your real funds or long‑term keys) when trying this; 3) do not provide private keys or secrets as env vars to untrusted code — manage keys in a secure wallet or hardware signer; 4) confirm the escrow API base URL (escrowapi.psiloai.com) is correct and owned by the service; and 5) ask the publisher for a package homepage, source repository, and an explicit list of environment variables/config paths the skill will read or write. If the publisher cannot provide those details, treat the skill as higher risk.
